correctness.rationale: For fixed-composition sampling, any prescribed p ones and q zeros at disjoint positions has hypergeometric probability (a)_p(b)_q/(a+b)_{p+q}. Partition the simultaneous singleton indicators by endpoint/interior and separation; prescribed local bit patterns give E X, E Y and E XY, with factoring Cov=2ab(a-1)(b-1)[ab(2n-3)-2n]/[n²(n-1)²(n-2)(n-3)]>0 using ab>=2(n-2). Given run counts and starting bit, one- and zero-run lengths are independent uniform compositions; expected singleton count in r parts summing to a is r(r-1)/(a-1). Even R fixes both run numbers and yields conditional independence. Odd R mixes two opposing endpoint orientations with weights C(a-1,t)C(b-1,t-1) and C(a-1,t-1)C(b-1,t), producing the negative covariance; t=1 simplifies to -4/(n-2)^2. The n=4,5 boundary cases are separately checked. Independent exact rational enumeration for all 2<=a,b<=7 agrees with both marginal and conditioned formulas.

value.rationale: In fixed-composition testing the per-color singleton-run counts are natural measures of isolated local symbols, and the total run count is the standard statistic used for conditioning. A uniform positive-to-nonpositive covariance reversal at every fixed run count, with strict sign at R=3, is an interpretable nontrivial dependence phenomenon. The exact algebra matters to run-stratified interpretation, without claiming a new downstream test.

final_claim: For a uniformly shuffled linear binary word with exactly a>=2 ones and b>=2 zeros, counts X,Y of singleton one- and zero-runs have strictly positive unconditional covariance but conditional covariance given any attainable number R of runs is <=0. It equals 0 when R is even, is the explicit negative two-orientation mixture when R=2t+1, and at R=3 equals -4/(a+b-2)^2.
limitations: Uniform fixed-composition linear binary words, a,b>=2; no cyclic, independent-unconditioned Bernoulli, or nonuniform analog.
